Let

\[
L_n=\frac{[(n+1)(n+2)\cdots(n+n)]^{1/n}}{n}
=\frac{\left(\prod_{k=n+1}^{2n} k\right)^{1/n}}{n}.
\]

Since \(L_n>0\), take natural logarithms:

\[
\ln L_n
=\frac1n\sum_{k=n+1}^{2n}\ln k-\ln n
=\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{k=n+1}^{2n}\ln k-n\ln n\right).
\]

Define

\[
u_n=\sum_{k=n+1}^{2n}\ln k-n\ln n,
\qquad v_n=n.
\]

Then

\[
\ln L_n=\frac{u_n}{v_n}.
\]

We apply the Cesàro–Stolz theorem. Since \(v_n=n\) is strictly increasing and \(v_n\to\infty\),

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{u_n}{v_n}
=
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{u_{n+1}-u_n}{v_{n+1}-v_n},
\]

provided the second limit exists. Here \(v_{n+1}-v_n=1\), so we need \(\lim_{n\to\infty}(u_{n+1}-u_n)\).

Now

\[
u_{n+1}-u_n
=
\sum_{k=n+2}^{2n+2}\ln k-\sum_{k=n+1}^{2n}\ln k
-(n+1)\ln(n+1)+n\ln n.
\]

The difference of the sums is

\[
\ln(2n+1)+\ln(2n+2)-\ln(n+1)
=\ln\bigl(2(2n+1)\bigr).
\]

Thus

\[
\begin{aligned}
u_{n+1}-u_n
&=\ln\bigl(2(2n+1)\bigr)-\bigl((n+1)\ln(n+1)-n\ln n\bigr)\\
&=\ln\bigl(2(2n+1)\bigr)-\ln(n+1)-n\ln\left(1+\frac1n\right)\\
&=\ln 2+\ln\left(\frac{2n+1}{n+1}\right)-n\ln\left(1+\frac1n\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

Taking the limit,

\[
\ln\left(\frac{2n+1}{n+1}\right)\to \ln 2,
\]

and

\[
n\ln\left(1+\frac1n\right)
=
\frac{\ln(1+1/n)}{1/n}\to 1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}(u_{n+1}-u_n)
=
\ln 2+\ln 2-1
=
2\ln 2-1.
\]

By Cesàro–Stolz,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{u_n}{n}
=
2\ln 2-1.
\]

Hence

\[
